articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Image Analysis for Transport Applications' (Digest No.035)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Image Analysis for Transport Applications
IEE Colloquium on Image Analysis for Transport Applications
abstract: Recent advances in computer vision technology and the falling prices of related devices has extended the use of video/CCTV by making it practical to automatically identify vehicles visually either online or off-line. The objective of the research is to develop a computer-vision based automatic vehicle identification system to achieve vehicle identification using optical character recognition (OCR) techniques. The work involves investigations into real-time automatic number-plate recognition and its extension to other aspects of road traffic monitoring and control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: License plate recognition technology for toll violation enforcement
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Image Analysis for Transport Applications
abstract: The equipment used for the Fastoll integrated toll collection system was the RIA-300 license plate reader, loaned by the 3M company. This is a compact stand-alone automatic system. The principal elements of the equipment are a strobe light source, a shuttered video camera and an image processor. The shuttered video camera is used to record a still frame of each vehicle's license plate. The processor module is a 68020 based image processor that controls the system and performs character recognition. It receives an RS-170 still-frame video signal from the camera, which is stored in memory in a 640*512 array of eight-bit values. If the software in the microprocessor-based controller locates a license plate within the digitized image, character recognition algorithms are used to read the plate. The testing and appraisal of the system are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Vehicle and pedestrian detection and tracking
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Image Analysis for Transport Applications
abstract: A fully automatic vision-based technique to extract traffic data from scenes of roadway is proposed. This involves the application of a scene analysis technique to find, identify and determine the coordinates of moving vehicles and pedestrians in each frame. The coordinates/time data are translated into a number of traffic flow parameters. A number of detection and tracking algorithms are implemented in the OCCAM language to run on a transputer-image processing system. The application of the MAT-transform as an aid for vehicle classification is investigated. The initial results are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The perception component of the VIEWS project
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Image Analysis for Transport Applications
abstract: The VIEWS (visual inspection and evaluation of wide-area scenes) project described seeks to use advanced visual processing for monitoring and surveillance tasks in traffic scenes, including typical road traffic and ground traffic at airports. The major objective of the project is to develop and demonstrate a system capable of interpreting complex traffic scenes in real-time. An important component of VIEWS is the establishment of support tools to assist in the knowledge acquisition stage, and to allow automatic 'compilation' of visual strategies at the time the application is defined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High speed image classification using transputer arrays
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Image Analysis for Transport Applications
abstract: Most image analysis tasks are computationally intensive and this is a particularly important factor in applications where a primary consideration is to maximise operational speeds. Transputer arrays provide an infrastructure for implementation of algorithms which can be matched quite closely to the inherent structural features embedded in typical task areas. The paper describes an approach to the specification of algorithms for image classification which embody a direct link with implementational considerations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Image Analysis for Transport Applications
abstract: Traffic Tracker is an electronic image processing system which processes TV pictures of road junctions in order to find the track of vehicles through the junction. The system is contained on three printed circuit boards which plug into an IBM PC compatible AT or 386 computer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low-cost image analysis for transport applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Image Analysis for Transport Applications
abstract: The work described forms part of a collaborative project, funded for a period of two years by the SERC, the aim of which is to develop algorithms which will provide high quality data for a wide range of transport applications. The work carried out at Napier Polytechnic is described, which covers the development and testing of algorithms which simulate neural networks and enable vehicles to be detected and classified. The development of the TULIP system at the University of Newcastle is presented. The current work within TORG involves the use of the TULIP system for pedestrian tracking. Finally IMPACTS, a system developed at University College London, is described and its use in traffic surveillance discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
